cohort: 344 pregnant women who visited selected hospitals in eastern Ethiopia.
finding: Khat chewing during pregnancy was significantly associated with a higher risk of preterm birth (aRR = 2.19) and low birth weight (aRR = 4.17).
mod_finding: Adjustment for cesarean delivery decreased the regression coefficient of khat chewing on preterm birth and low birth weight, suggesting it plays a role as a confounder or mediator in the observed associations.
